To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the levels of PCDD/F and PCB in livers of sheep are strongly influenced by the levels in the feed, but that the kinetics are complex and that levels in meat and fat remain well below the MLs.
the levels of PCDD/F and PCBs in sheep liver and kidney fat can increase rapidly when sheep are exposed to contaminated feed.

the intake of PCDD/F and PCBs in sheep can result in levels in livers exceeding the new MLs in the EU and in meat exceeding the MLs for meat, but that these levels decrease again to the levels in control animals within a few weeks after the intake has been stopped.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behavior of these persistent contaminants in sheep, which can be used to assess the risk to human health.
the accumulation of PCDD/F and PCBs in the liver, fat and muscle tissue of sheep and their kinetics in response to a short term exposure.
the accumulation of PCDD/F and PCBs in livers and the kinetics of their elimination after exposure to a contaminated diet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the levels of PCDD/F in the livers of the young sheep exceeded the new MLs, whereas the PCBs did not.
PCDD/Fs and PCBs are accumulated in sheep livers and other organs.
the levels of the various contaminants in the tissues are related to the intake of the contaminants in the food, but that this relationship is not straightforward.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the levels of PCDD/F in livers of sheep are very high, but that they are not toxicologically relevant.
the new product based maximum limits in the EU will be exceeded in sheep livers, especially for PCDD/Fs, but not for PCBs.
the levels in the livers of the sheep exceeded the new MLs and that these were already present at the start of exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the levels of PCDD/F and PCBs in livers are not only determined by the current intake but are also influenced by the intake over a long period, and this is particularly true for the higher chlorinated compounds.

the levels of PCDD/F and PCB in sheep liver can be increased to levels above the current EU MLs, and that this can be achieved by feeding the animals with grass contaminated at 2.4 times the maximum level of PCDD/F.
sheep liver is a major sink for PCDD/Fs and PCBs and that their intake is not reflected in the meat and fat.
